pr_body:
This is a variation on `Buffer.from(arrayBufferView)` that copies the bytes and does not truncate when using a multibyte TypedArray.  For instance,

```
Buffer.from(new Uint16Array([0xffff]))
<Buffer ff>

Buffer.copyBytesFrom(new Uint16Array([0xffff]))
<Buffer ff ff> 
```

Open to suggestions on a better name.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/43862
pr_comments: Counter-suggestion: Mark `Buffer` as a legacy API? There's no good reason for not using standardized equivalents in 2023.

> Mark Buffer as a legacy API? There's no good reason for not using standardized equivalents in 2023.

As much as I do prefer standardized APIs, Buffer clearly is never ever going to decline in use and is being actively implemented and used in at least three other runtimes right now. It's not going anywhere and there's really no benefit I think to changing it's status

Is there a reason to work with `TypedArray` and not `ArrayBufferView` (which also includes `DataView`)?

`TypedArray.from` is basically a variant of `Array.from` and therefore requires iterable value as first parameter, but it should be irrelevant for this method.
@LiviaMedeiros ... the implementation does use `ArrayBufferView`. I've updated the doc change to reflect that.

> @LiviaMedeiros ... the implementation does use `ArrayBufferView`. I've updated the doc change to reflect that.

How do we interpret `length` for `DataView`s? As the number of 8-bit chunks? Or 32-bit chunks? Same questions for `offset`. Whatever we chose, it would feel quite arbitrary to me, I’d rather have us only support `TypedArray`, and maybe `DataView` only if `length` and `offset` are not supplied.

Yeah, I realized that the `DataView` wouldn't work with the current implementation anyway. Let's limit it to `TypedArray`. I don't really like the idea of supporting `DataView` only part of the time, and would rather just make it consistent no matter what other arguments are passed in.

> How do we interpret `length` for `DataView`s? As the number of 8-bit chunks? Or 32-bit chunks? Same questions for `offset`.

It might be reasonable to interpret both as number of bytes, and `length` can become `byteLength`.
This would also remove limitation of having to copy full chunks.

I'm not quite sure if there are usecases of copy where counting elements is preferred over counting bytes and at the same time it wouldn't be better to process elements on copy (i.e. by using `TypedArray.from(arrayLike, mapFn)` which also can be ported to `Buffer`).

> I'm not quite sure if there are usecases of copy where counting elements is preferred over counting bytes

Well the existence of [`%TypedArray.prototype%.slice`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray/slice) seems to indicate that's the use case the spec authors thought was the most common.


> This would also remove limitation of having to copy full chunks.

I think that when folks are using say `Uint16Array`, they intend to work only with 16-bit chunks, otherwise they would be using something else. The limitation is a feature, not a bug IMHO.

> Well the existence of [`%TypedArray.prototype%.slice`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray/slice) seems to indicate that's the use case the spec authors thought was the most common.

Yes, this is indeed a part of `TypedArray.prototype` inheriting most of `Array.prototype` methods.

> I think that when folks are using say `Uint16Array`, they intend to work only with 16-bit chunks, otherwise they would be using something else. The limitation is a feature, not a bug IMHO.

On the contrary, in context of `Buffer` and this method we want to switch from array-like structure of typed elements to uniform bytearray, so we don't need to care how the original value was built and used.
In particular, the fact that this method reinterprets values of `Float##Array` into unsigned chars indicates that we work with raw buffer.

A common usecase for this method might be expanding any APIs accepting `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` arguments into accepting arbitrary views; and if we need to extract a particular slice, using `byteLength` and byte-based `offset` might allow us to skip recalculating (since `Buffer.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT === 1` and therefore `desiredLength === desiredByteLength === sourceSliceByteLength`).
And in cases when we deal with specific `TypedArray` for known specific reasons, we are likely to prefer calling `.slice()` directly and process typed elements without conversion to `Buffer`.

issue_context.title: Buffer.from(`<ArrayBufferView>`)
issue_context.body:
### What is the problem this feature will solve?

[`Buffer.from()`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#static-method-bufferfromarray) has many different forms, including [`Buffer.from(arrayBuffer[, byteOffset[, length]])`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#static-method-bufferfromarraybuffer-byteoffset-length) and [`Buffer.from(buffer)`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#static-method-bufferfrombuffer).

However, `Buffer.from(abv)` does not exist. Depending on exact input, trying to call it with such objects results in false positives, data truncation, data corruption (e.g. `double` -> `unsigned char`), thrown `TypeError`s and empty buffers.

Creating `Buffer` from `ArrayBufferView`'s data in userland is extremely error-prone because `Buffer.from(arrayBuffer)` doesn't copy the data.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Adjust `Buffer.from(buffer)` to accept not only `Buffer` and `Uint8Array` but any `ArrayBufferView` or at least any `TypedArray`.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Deprecation and removal of `Buffer` from core into userspace module, with prior porting all core APIs to native `Uint8Array`/`TypedArray`/`ArrayBufferView`s.

There has been no activity on this feature request for 5 months and it is unlikely to be implemented. It will be closed 6 months after the last non-automated comment.

For more information on how the project manages feature requests, please consult the [feature request management document](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/HEAD/doc/contributing/feature-request-management.md).
This should be kept open. It's still needed
@jasnell Is this _actionable_, though? `Buffer.from(abv)` has well-defined semantics right now (even if those include data truncation – it matches `Uint8Array.from()` in that regard, afaict).
It doesn't need to be `Buffer.from(abv)` exactly. It can easily be another variation, `Buffer.fromTypedArray` or such (I'm horrible with naming so other suggestions are welcome)

Yeah, we could do that. It’s probably worth thinking about the name – it should reflect that it creates the buffer from the underlying memory of a TypedArray rather than its contents – and it’s probably still worth thinking about whether this really makes sense to address in Node.js itself (the fact that writing `new Uint8Array(typedArray.buffer, typedArray.byteOffset, typedArray.byteLength)` is verbose and repetitive isn’t really a Node.js-specific thing).
Agreed with idea of separate method; its existence by itself would also imply that `Buffer.from(abv)` does something different.

review_comments: Note that we _could_ defer on `TypedArrayPrototypeGetLength` to check wether `view` is a `TypedArray` or not as it would throw a `TypeError: Method get TypedArray.prototype.length called on incompatible receiver` anyway. But I get why we would prefer to have a Node.js specific error for consistency.
Yeah, I'd rather have the consistent `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` error
